summary: US equities retreated Thursday as surging oil prices above $102/bbl and climbing Treasury yields reignited stagflation fears, halting a rally that had pushed major indexes to new records earlier this week. The Nasdaq led declines, falling over 1.4% intraday after the Financial Times reported OpenAI's annualized revenue is roughly $20 billion lower than previously estimated, triggering a sharp selloff in semiconductor stocks. Meanwhile, crypto markets extended their slide as Bitcoin and Ethereum ETFs logged significant outflows—Bitcoin funds shed $487 million on Wednesday while Ethereum ETFs bled for a seventh consecutive session with $202 million in withdrawals. Rising rates and a stronger dollar are pressuring both risk assets, with the 10-year Treasury yield hovering near 5.3% amid persistent inflation concerns. Fed commentary remains hawkish, though Chair Kevin Warsh's tenure is still nascent following the contentious transition from Powell, who is staying on the Board as a governor amid legal battles over central bank independence.

signals.title: OpenAI revenue shortfall sparks chip stock rout
signals.desc: Financial Times reported OpenAI's annualized revenue is $20 billion below prior estimates, sending semiconductor stocks down 3% and dragging Nasdaq 100 lower by 1.3%.

signals.title: Bitcoin and Ethereum ETFs see heavy outflows
signals.desc: Bitcoin spot ETFs recorded $487 million in outflows Wednesday while Ethereum ETFs extended losses to seven straight sessions with $202 million withdrawn, signaling fading institutional demand.

signals.title: Oil surge above $102 revives stagflation fears
signals.desc: Brent crude climbed above $102/bbl on escalating Middle East tensions, pressuring equity valuations and reigniting concerns over energy-driven inflation amid already elevated Treasury yields.

signals.title: 10-year Treasury yield near 5.3% weighs on growth stocks
signals.desc: Bond yields remain stubbornly high at 5.31% on the 10-year as markets price persistent inflation and reduced Fed easing expectations, narrowing the runway for tech multiple expansion.

signals.title: Jobless claims data due at 8:30 AM ET
signals.desc: Initial jobless claims expected at 200K with continuing claims at 1.71M; constructive print could stabilize sentiment, but labor market cooling without recession remains the Fed's base case.

verdict: Risk-off tone prevails as oil shock, rising yields, and AI revenue skepticism outweigh recent momentum; defensive posture warranted into jobless claims and month-end earnings.
